This is almost always a mechanical issue with the turntable drive, not the heating system. 1. 2. The roller ring underneath has become dirty or dislodged.
3. The turntable motor itself has failed (less common, but possible). Before we look at parts, let's check the simple stuff first. Please unplug the microwave for safety. - Is the small three-pronged coupler in the centre cracked or loose?
• Is the roller ring underneath clean and intact?
• When you put it back, does it sit flat without catching on anything? Let me know what you find with those checks.
ok unplugged. the plastic 3 pronged bit in the middle has a crack and the hole looks rounded. roller ring is in place and the wheels turn fine. plate sits on it but wobbles

The crack and rounded hole in the central three-pronged coupler is most likely the cause. That part transfers the rotation from the motor to your plate; because it’s cracked and worn, it slips instead of turning the tray, which leaves one side of your food cold. You will need a replacement turntable coupler (sometimes sold as part of a 'turntable repair kit' with rollers). Check if that is just because the coupler isn't holding it level, or if the glass tray itself has a chip/crack on its underside. If the glass is intact, checking the coupler should fix the rotation and the uneven heating. 1. Ensure the microwave is still unplugged.
2. Remove the roller ring and lift out the glass plate.
3. Pull off the old cracked coupler from the central spindle.
4. Fit the new coupler firmly onto the spindle.
5. Replace the roller ring, then set the glass plate back on top so it sits flat.
6. Plug in and test. If you can't find a specific coupler for your model, look for a universal turntable repair kit that includes a compatible coupler and rollers.
